summary: 24-year-old man after an alcohol binge: repeated retching, then a streak of fresh blood in the vomit; normal observations, Hb 14.8, urea 5.2 (GBS 0). Most tears stop spontaneously; outpatient management.

inputs.hpi: Heavy drinking last night. Vomited repeatedly this morning; after several episodes of forceful retching there were streaks of fresh red blood in the vomit, about a teaspoon. No further vomiting for 3 hours. Stools normal. No chest pain, no breathlessness. No medications.

exam.general: Well, hydrated. Pulse 88/min, BP 126/80. No surgical emphysema.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness. PR: brown stool.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Mallory-Weiss tear
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Probable Mallory-Weiss tear after retching; small-volume haematemesis, Glasgow-Blatchford 0.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 3 of ios.bayes: 1. Acute Pancreatitis | 2. Upper GI Bleeding (Peptic Ulcer) | 3. Oesophageal Variceal Bleeding | 4. Acute Kidney Injury | 5. Small Bowel Obstruction

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Emergency now (score 120): any "blood"/"bleed" word is an urgent red flag regardless of volume or GBS, and "No chest pain" in the HPI fires "Possible cardiac event" (adaptiveTriage reads CC+HPI free text without negation).
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: adaptive-triage: grade GI bleeding by haemodynamics/GBS instead of the word; add negation handling ("no …", "denies …") before RED_FLAGS matching.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: GBS ≤1: outpatient management without early endoscopy; endoscopic haemostasis only for actively bleeding Mallory-Weiss tears; tranexamic acid not recommended
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: ACG Clinical Guideline — upper gastrointestinal and ulcer bleeding
guideline.citation: Laine L, Barkun AN, Saltzman JR, Martel M, Leontiadis GI. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:899–917.

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Classic low-risk Mallory-Weiss tear. Tests that the specific diagnosis is offered, that the bleed is not escalated to "emergency now", and that the plan stays supportive. The absent chest pain and surgical emphysema separate it from Boerhaave (see boerhaave-* vignettes).
